Production is upgraded one release at a time. Ops can roll any release back to
the previous one, so **each release must read everything its neighbours
write**: no deploy and no rollback may sign anyone out or break a link in a
mail that was already sent. Keep these notes up to date with every release of
the upgrade.

## Releases

| Release | Ruby | Rails | Bundle | Framework defaults | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R0 | 3.0.7 | 6.1.7.10 | `Gemfile` | legacy (no `load_defaults`) | previous production release |
| **R1** | **3.2.9** | **6.1.7.10** | `Gemfile` | legacy + 1 temporary override | **this release** |
| R2 | 3.2.9 | 7.0.8.7 | `Gemfile.next` (becomes `Gemfile`) | `load_defaults 7.0` | next release, prepared here |

R1 is the rollback target of R2, so it has to read what Rails 7.0 writes on
its framework defaults. R2 must not need any rollback-related override.

## Dual boot

`Gemfile.next` evaluates `Gemfile` with `next?` returning true; only the
dependencies switched on `next?` differ (Rails, and
activerecord-sqlserver-adapter). Each bundle has its own lockfile.

    bundle install && bin/rails test                     # Rails 6.1 (production)
    BUNDLE_GEMFILE=Gemfile.next bundle install           # Rails 7.0 (Gemfile.next.lock)
    BUNDLE_GEMFILE=Gemfile.next bin/rails test

`config/application.rb` loads `config.load_defaults 7.0` on Rails 7, so the
`Gemfile.next` build runs exactly the configuration R2 will ship. CI
(`.github/workflows/tests.yml`) runs both bundles on Ruby 3.2. Code that has to
differ between the versions is switched on the Rails version, never on the
release.

## R1: Ruby 3.2, Rails 6.1 (this release)

### Changes

* `.ruby-version` is 3.2.9 and `Gemfile.lock` is locked on Ruby 3.2.9 with
  Bundler 2.4.19 (the one shipped with Ruby 3.2; 2.2.33 prints deprecation
  warnings on 3.2). Only nokogiri changed (1.15.7 -> 1.18.9, already selected
  by the Gemfile for Ruby >= 3.1) besides platform suffixes. Rails stays
  6.1.7.10. No application change was needed for Ruby 3.2.
* No database migration: a rollback to R0 needs no down-migration. R0 is
  rolled back with its own build (Ruby 3.0.7 and its `Gemfile.lock`).
* `Gemfile.next` / `Gemfile.next.lock`: Rails 7.0.8.7, every other gem at
  the version of `Gemfile.lock`.
* Changes needed by Rails 7.0, harmless on 6.1:
  * `config/initializers/10-patches.rb`: the lookup of the `*.api.rsb` API
    templates relied on 6.1 resolver internals. On Rails 7.0 the `api`
    format is added to the template path parser and to the details key, and
    the rendered template keeps no format of its own (as on 6.1) so that the
    response is in the requested xml/json format.
  * `to_s(:db)` -> `to_formatted_s(:db)` (test fixtures, query test):
    `load_defaults 7.0` disables the `to_s(format)` override.
  * `ApplicationController#redirect_to_referer_or` passes
    `allow_other_host: true`: it keeps following the referer as before,
    `raise_on_open_redirects` (7.0 default) raised on referers it could not
    parse. Ignored by Rails 6.1.
  * `config.active_record.belongs_to_required_by_default = false` on Rails
    7.0: permanent application choice (Redmine validates its associations
    itself), not related to rollback.

### What each release writes and reads

| | R0 writes | R1 writes | R2 writes | R1 reads |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Session cookie cipher | AES-256-CBC + HMAC | AES-256-CBC + HMAC | AES-256-GCM | both |
| Cookie key derivation (PBKDF2) | SHA1 | SHA1 | SHA256 | both |
| Session serialization | Marshal | **JSON** | JSON | both |
| Cookie purpose metadata | no | no | yes | both |
| CSRF tokens in forms | global | global | per-form | both |
| Mail link tokens (`message_verifier`) | SHA1 key | SHA1 key | SHA256 key | both |
| Cache entries | 6.1 format | 6.1 format | 7.0 format | both |

* R0 reads what R1 writes: R0 decrypts SHA1/CBC cookies, and its `:marshal`
  cookie serializer falls back to JSON (`MarshalWithJsonFallback` in Rails
  6.1). Global CSRF tokens, SHA1 mail links and 6.1 cache entries are what
  R0 itself writes.
* R2 reads what R1 writes thanks to the SHA1 rotations of
  `config/initializers/15-release_compatibility.rb` (loaded on Rails 7.0 as
  well) and to R1 writing JSON sessions. Rails 7.0 reads 6.1 cache entries
  and global CSRF tokens natively.

### Temporary framework-default override (R1 only)

* `config.action_dispatch.cookies_serializer = :hybrid` (Rails 6.1 branch
  of `config/application.rb`). Reads Marshal (R0) and JSON (R2) cookies,
  writes JSON. R2 uses `:json` (7.0 default) and cannot read Marshal; R0 can
  read JSON, so JSON is the only format all three read. Every session used
  while R1 runs is converted. Goes away with the Rails 6.1 branch in R2.

Newer framework defaults (5.0 to 7.0) are deliberately **not** adopted in R1,
which keeps running without `load_defaults`; R1 only learns to *read* what
they produce:

* SHA256 key derivation and `cache_format_version ",
  "output_tail": "ng release's derivation, verifies SHA1 and SHA256 tokens.
* **Per-form CSRF tokens** are accepted even when not issued (Rails 6.1),
  so forms rendered by R2 can be submitted after a rollback. Tokens for
  another form are still rejected. R1 keeps issuing global tokens.
* **Rails 7.0 cache entries** are read on Rails 6.1 (file, redis, memcache
  stores). Without it a file store misses with an error and a 6.1 memcache
  store would return the binary payload as the cached value (eg. formatted
  wiki text).

Session data must survive JSON (symbol keys become strings):
`QueriesHelper#query_session_data` restores the issue/time entry query data
kept in the session; `AccountController#register` reads the LDAP on-the-fly
registration data with indifferent access. After a rollback to R0, R0 reads
these JSON sessions without signing anyone out but resets a query kept in the
session to its defaults once, and an LDAP on-the-fly registration in progress
has to be restarted. Plugins storing other objects in the session must keep
them JSON compatible.

### Verification

* Test suite (`test/unit`, `functional`, `integration`, `helpers`,
  `generators`) on Ruby 3.2: 5328 runs, 0 failures, 0 errors on `Gemfile`
  (Rails 6.1) and on `Gemfile.next` (Rails 7.0, `load_defaults 7.0`); 41
  skips, as before, plus 4 version-specific ones on Rails 7.0. R0 baseline
  on Ruby 3.0: 5308 runs (without generators), 0 failures.
* `test/integration/release_compatibility_test.rb` and
  `test/unit/release_compatibility_keys_and_cache_test.rb` build the
  cookies, CSRF tokens, mail link tokens and cache entries of the other
  releases from scratch and run on both bundles.
* End-to-end check in production mode with a shared database, secret and
  file cache, R0 on Ruby 3.0, R1 and R2 on Ruby 3.2: session, form
  submission, mail link and cache entry carried over R0 -> R1, R1 -> R0,
  R1 -> R2, R2 -> R1, and the session over R0 -> R1 -> R2 and
  R2 -> R1 -> R0. All pass. Without the compatibility code every R1 <-> R2
  case fails except R2 reading R1's cache entries (Rails 7.0 reads the 6.1
  format natively).

### Known limitations

* A session cookie written by R0 and not used while R1 runs cannot be read
  by R2 (Marshal); its user is signed out unless they have an autologin
  cookie. See the ship gate below.
* Rolling back two releases (R2 -> R1 -> R0) is only safe for what went
  through R1: R0 cannot read sessions created on R2 and not used on R1, nor
  verify links mailed by R2 in the last 30 days, and its cache reads R2's
  entries as errors (file store) or garbage (memcache). Clear the cache
  (`bin/rake tmp:cache:clear` / flush memcache) when rolling back to R0
  after R2 ran.
* ETags and long cache keys are digested with MD5 on R1 and SHA256 on R2
  (`hash_digest_class`): one-time cache misses / full responses, no
  functional impact.
* Jobs: the production queue adapter is `:async` (in memory), nothing is
  persisted across releases. Revisit if a persistent queue is introduced.

## Work left for R2 (Rails 7.0 on its framework defaults)

1. Make Rails 7.0 the production bundle: copy `Gemfile.next.lock` to

5. Ship gate: R1 must have run in production for at least the session

6. Rails 7.1 deprecations seen under 7.0, to fix before moving on:

   `ActiveSupport::SafeBuffer` (call `to_s`).

  can go entirely.
* The next Rails version (7.1) changes formats again (message serializer and
  metadata, cache format 7.1...): R2 will have to be prepared as its
  rollback target the same way.

# Compatibility between adjacent releases of the Rails 6.1 -> 7.0 upgrade.
#
# Every release must be able to read what the release before it and the
# release after it write, so that neither a deploy nor a rollback signs anyone
# out or breaks a link in a mail that was already sent:
#
# * session cookies (encrypted cookie jar) and signed cookies,
# * links signed with Rails.application.message_verifier (Mailer.mail_link_token),
# * CSRF tokens of the forms already rendered in browsers,
# * entries of a cache store shared between releases.
#
# This file is loaded both on Rails 6.1 (Gemfile, production) and on Rails 7.0
# with its framework defaults (Gemfile.next, next release). It never changes
# the format written by the running release, it only lets it read the other
# formats. See docs/UPGRADE.md for the details and for when each part can go.
module RedmineApp
  module ReleaseCompatibility
    # Rails derives the secrets of cookies and message verifiers from
    # secret_key_base with PBKDF2 (1000 iterations, see
    # Rails::Application#key_generator). Rails 6.1 always hashes with SHA1,
    # Rails 7.0 on its defaults with SHA256
    # (config.active_support.key_generator_hash_digest_class).
    KEY_DERIVATION_DIGESTS = [OpenSSL::Digest::SHA1, OpenSSL::Digest::SHA256].freeze
    KEY_DERIVATION_ITERATIONS = 1000

    # Same keys as ActiveSupport::KeyGenerator, with an explicit digest
    # (ActiveSupport 6.1 has no hash_digest_class option).
    class KeyGenerator
      attr_reader :digest

      def initialize(secret, digest)
        @secret = secret
        @digest = digest
        @keys = Concurrent::Map.new
      end

      def generate_key(salt, key_size=64)
        @keys.compute_if_absent([salt, key_size]) do
          OpenSSL::PKCS5.pbkdf2_hmac(@secret, salt, KEY_DERIVATION_ITERATIONS, key_size, @digest.new)
        end
      end
    end

    class << self
      def key_generators(secret)
        KEY_DERIVATION_DIGESTS.map {|digest| KeyGenerator.new(secret, digest)}
      end

      # Adds rotations to the cookie jars for the cookie formats written by
      # the releases of the upgrade:
      # * Rails 6.1 on legacy defaults: AES-256-CBC + HMAC, SHA1 derived keys
      # * Rails 7.0 on its defaults: AES-256-GCM, SHA256 derived keys
      # Rails decrypts with the format of the running release first and
      # rewrites a cookie read with a rotation in that format.
      def add_cookie_rotations(config, key_generators)
        rotations = config.cookies_rotations
        gcm, cbc = 'aes-256-gcm', 'aes-256-cbc'
        key_generators.each do |generator|
          rotations.rotate(

            :digest => config.cookies_digest || 'SHA1'
          )

#   cookies, JSON payloads with purpose metadata, per-form CSRF tokens.
#
# Runs on Rails 6.1 (Gemfile) and on Rails 7.0 (Gemfile.next).
class ReleaseCompatibilityTest < Redmine::IntegrationTest
  fixtures :projects, :users, :email_addresses, :roles, :members, :member_roles,

  NULL_SERIALIZER = ActiveSupport::MessageEncryptor::NullSerializer

  def rails70?

  def derive_key(salt, digest, key_size=64)
    OpenSSL::PKCS5.pbkdf2_hmac(Rails.application.secret_key_base, salt, 1000, key_size, digest.new)
  end

  def rails70_encryptor

      :cipher => 'aes-256-gcm', :serializer => NULL_SERIALIZER
    )

require "active_support/core_ext/kernel/reporting"
require "active_support/notifications"

module ActiveSupport
  module Messages # :nodoc:
    module SerializerWithFallback # :nodoc:
      def self.[](format)
        if format.to_s.include?("message_pack") && !defined?(ActiveSupport::MessagePack)
          require "active_support/message_pack"
        end

        SERIALIZERS.fetch(format)
      end

      def load(dumped)
        format = detect_format(dumped)

        if format == self.format
          _load(dumped)
        elsif format && fallback?(format)
          payload = { serializer: SERIALIZERS.key(self), fallback: format, serialized: dumped }
          ActiveSupport::Notifications.instrument("message_serializer_fallback.active_support", payload) do
            payload[:deserialized] = SERIALIZERS[format]._load(dumped)
          end
        else
          raise "Unsupported serialization format"
        end
      end

      private
        def detect_format(dumped)
          case
          when MessagePackWithFallback.dumped?(dumped)
            :message_pack
          when MarshalWithFallback.dumped?(dumped)
            :marshal
          when JsonWithFallback.dumped?(dumped)
            :json
          end
        end

        def fallback?(format)
          format != :marshal
        end

        module AllowMarshal
          private
            def fallback?(format)
              super || format == :marshal
            end
        end

        module MarshalWithFallback
          include SerializerWithFallback
          extend self

          def format
            :marshal
          end

          def dump(object)
            Marshal.dump(object)
          end

          def _load(dumped)
            Marshal.load(dumped)
          end

          MARSHAL_SIGNATURE = "\x04\x08"

          def dumped?(dumped)
            dumped.start_with?(MARSHAL_SIGNATURE)
          end
        end

        module JsonWithFallback
          include SerializerWithFallback
          extend self

          def format
            :json
          end

          def dump(object)
            ActiveSupport::JSON.encode(object)
          end

          def _load(dumped)
            ActiveSupport::JSON.decode(dumped)
          end

          JSON_START_WITH = /\A(?:[{\["]|-?\d|true|false|null)/

          def dumped?(dumped)
            JSON_START_WITH.match?(dumped)
          end

          private
            def detect_format(dumped)
              super || :json
            end
        end

        module JsonWithFallbackAllowMarshal
          include JsonWithFallback
          include AllowMarshal
          extend self
        end

        module MessagePackWithFallback
          include SerializerWithFallback
          extend self

          def format
            :message_pack
          end

          def dump(object)
            ActiveSupport::MessagePack.dump(object)
          end

          def _load(dumped)
            ActiveSupport::MessagePack.load(dumped)
          end

          def dumped?(dumped)
            available? && ActiveSupport::MessagePack.signature?(dumped)
          end

          private
            def available?
              return @available if defined?(@available)
              silence_warnings { require "active_support/message_pack" }
              @available = true
            rescue LoadError
              @available = false
            end
        end

        module MessagePackWithFallbackAllowMarshal
          include MessagePackWithFallback
          include AllowMarshal
          extend self
        end

        SERIALIZERS = {
          marshal: MarshalWithFallback,
          json: JsonWithFallback,
          json_allow_marshal: JsonWithFallbackAllowMarshal,
          message_pack: MessagePackWithFallback,
          message_pack_allow_marshal: MessagePackWithFallbackAllowMarshal,
        }
    end
  end
end

Checking cookie_metadata and the MessageEncryptor format in 7.2 against 7.0, both the purpose string and GCM encoding layout line up the same way, so cookies should transfer natively between versions. That means the real compatibility risks are the message verifier used for mail links and any AR marshalling in caches, not the cookie jar itself — so next I want to diff request_forgery_protection token generation between 7.0.8.7 and 7.2.4.

Found that in 7.2 the cookie jar encrypts with `NullSerializer`, so cookies still use the legacy 7.0 metadata envelope, meaning they should be natively compatible—I'll verify this empirically. Next I'll compare CSRF token handling between 7.0 and 7.2.

I'm noting that the R1 compat override for per-form CSRF token validation just delegates to super when per_form_csrf_tokens is enabled on 7.0/7.2, so it's effectively inactive and safe to remove in R2 per the notes.

Now I'm digging into how session CSRF tokens are stored and encoded across versions — same session key `_csrf_token` is used throughout, but 6.1-era defaults write non-urlsafe base64 while 7.0+ defaults (urlsafe_csrf_tokens = true) expect urlsafe encoding. I'm confirming that `Base64.urlsafe_decode64` still correctly decodes standard base64 strings containing '+' and '/', since it only translates '-' and '_' and leaves other characters alone — which explains why Rails could make this change without breaking old sessions.

Next I want to check per-form token validation for relative action paths — specifically whether `normalize_relative_action_path` behaves differently between the versions when validating against `request.path.chomp('/')`, since Redmine forms mostly use absolute paths but edge cases with relative actions could matter. I need to compare the actual implementations side by side to see if the normalization logic diverged.

    class Coder # :nodoc:
      def initialize(serializer, compressor, legacy_serializer: false)
        @serializer = serializer
        @compressor = compressor
        @legacy_serializer = legacy_serializer
      end

      def dump(entry)
        return @serializer.dump(entry) if @legacy_serializer

        dump_compressed(entry, Float::INFINITY)
      end

      def dump_compressed(entry, threshold)
        return @serializer.dump_compressed(entry, threshold) if @legacy_serializer

        if type = type_for_string(entry.value)
          payload = entry.value.b
        else
          type = OBJECT_DUMP_TYPE
          payload = @serializer.dump(entry.value)
        end

        if compressed = try_compress(payload, threshold)
          payload = compressed
          type = type | COMPRESSED_FLAG
        end

        expires_at = entry.expires_at || -1.0

        version = dump_version(entry.version) if entry.version
        version_length = version&.bytesize || -1

        packed = SIGNATURE.b
        packed << [type, expires_at, version_length].pack(PACKED_TEMPLATE)
        packed << version if version
        packed << payload
      end

        type = dumped.unpack1(PACKED_TYPE_TEMPLATE)
        expires_at = dumped.unpack1(PACKED_EXPIRES_AT_TEMPLATE)
        version_length = dumped.unpack1(PACKED_VERSION_LENGTH_TEMPLATE)

        expires_at = nil if expires_at < 0
        version = load_version(dumped.byteslice(PACKED_VERSION_INDEX, version_length)) if version_length >= 0
        payload = dumped.byteslice((PACKED_VERSION_INDEX + [version_length, 0].max)..)

        serializer = STRING_DESERIALIZERS[type & ~COMPRESSED_FLAG] || @serializer

      end

        SIGNATURE = "\x00\x11".b.freeze

        OBJECT_DUMP_TYPE = 0x01

        STRING_ENCODINGS = {
          0x02 => Encoding::UTF_8,
          0x03 => Encoding::BINARY,
          0x04 => Encoding::US_ASCII,

        COMPRESSED_FLAG = 0x80

        PACKED_TEMPLATE = "CEl<"
        PACKED_TYPE_TEMPLATE = "@#{SIGNATURE.bytesize}C"
        PACKED_EXPIRES_AT_TEMPLATE = "@#{[0].pack(PACKED_TYPE_TEMPLATE).bytesize}E"

steps.reasoning_content:
I'm tracing how the 7.2 Coder detects raw Marshal signatures versus falling back through SerializerWithFallback, which then recognizes the older 7.0 marker bytes and unpacks the cache entry via marshal_load.

For 6.1 entries though, dumped? returns true for raw Marshal, so it loads directly into a Marshal-deserialized object whose ivar shape (value, version, created_at vs expires_in, compressed flag) may not match what 7.2's Entry class expects — this is the trickier cross-version compatibility case I need to work through, particularly whether compressed? still resolves correctly against the old ivar names.

I'm tracing how the payload gets serialized and compressed, then checking what happens when the older 7.0 coder tries to read a 7.2-format entry — it would hit a Marshal version mismatch and raise a TypeError, so I need to figure out how that failure actually gets handled downstream.

For the deserialize_entry path, that error isn't caught by the rescue for DeserializationError, so it propagates up to read_entry. For FileStore, this just gets logged as an error and treated as a cache miss, so the behavior is relatively graceful there — but I still need to check how the Memcache store handles the same failure case.

Now I'm digging into the 7.0 format for MemCacheStore and thinking through a compatibility layer for reading 7.1-format entries. The tricky part is that the 7.1 signature happens to start with the same byte the 7.0 format uses to mark uncompressed Marshal data, so a naive reader could misinterpret a 7.1 entry as corrupted 7.0 data. I need the compat check to look for the full 7.1 signature before falling back to the 7.0 Marshal path, and I'm verifying whether a genuine 7.0 entry could ever collide with that same byte sequence.

I'll look at how 7.0's file/memcache/redis stores deserialize data to find where to add support for reading the 7.1 format.

        Module.new do
          def build_path_regex
            handlers = Regexp.union(Template::Handlers.extensions.map(&:to_s))
            formats = Regexp.union(Template::Types.symbols.map(&:to_s) + ['api'])

            regular_locales = [/[a-z]{2}(?:[-_][A-Z]{2})?/]
            locales = Regexp.union(available_locales + regular_locales)
            variants = "[^.]*"

            %r{
              \A
              (?:(?<prefix>.*)/)?
              (?<partial>_)?
              (?<action>.*?)
              (?:\.(?<locale>#{locales}))??
              (?:\.(?<format>#{formats}))??
              (?:\+(?<variant>#{variants}))??
              (?:\.(?<handler>#{handlers}))?

        end

      # response gets the requested one (xml or json).

        Module.new do
          def format_or_default

      # TemplateDetails::Requested), so the key has to include :api too.
      # LookupContext::DetailsKey drops unregistered formats, hence this cache.

            if File.exist? path

Then I'm tracing how a Rails 7.1 cache entry gets decoded from its binary payload - unpacking the type byte, expiration timestamp, and version length from fixed offsets, then extracting the version string and the remaining payload data by byte slicing.

If the compression flag is set, it inflates the payload with zlib before clearing that bit from the type. # See config/initializers/15-release_compatibility.rb and docs/UPGRADE.md.
# Runs on Rails 6.1 (Gemfile) and on Rails 7.0 (Gemfile.next).
class ReleaseCompatibilityKeysAndCacheTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  def setup
    @cache_dir = Dir.mktmpdir
    @store = ActiveSupport::Cache::FileStore.new(@cache_dir)
  end

  def teardown
    FileUtils.rm_rf(@cache_dir)
  end

  def rails70?
    Rails::VERSION::MAJOR >= 7
  end

  def cache_file(key)
    @store.send(:normalize_key, key, {})
  end

  def write_cache_payload(key, payload)
    path = cache_file(key)
    FileUtils.mkdir_p(File.dirname(path))
    File.binwrite(path, payload)
  end

  # Cache payload as written by Rails 7.0 on its defaults (cache_format_version 7.0)
  def rails70_cache_payload(value, expires_at: nil, version: nil, compress: false)
    members = [value, expires_at, version]
    members.pop while !members.empty? && members.last.nil?
    payload = Marshal.dump(members)
    compress ? "\x01".b + Zlib::Deflate.deflate(payload) : "\x00".b + payload
  end

  def test_cache_entry_written_by_rails70_on_its_defaults_is_read
    write_cache_payload 'plain', rails70_cache_payload('formatted text')
    write_cache_payload 'compressed', rails70_cache_payload('x' * 5000, :compress => true)
    write_cache_payload 'versioned', rails70_cache_payload(%w(a b), :version => 'v1', :expires_at => 1.hour.from_now.to_f)

    assert_equal 'formatted text', @store.read('plain')
    assert_equal 'x' * 5000, @store.read('compressed')
    assert_equal %w(a b), @store.read('versioned', :version => 'v1')
    assert_nil @store.read('versioned', :version => 'v2')
  end

  def test_expired_cache_entry_written_by_rails70_on_its_defaults_is_ignored
    write_cache_payload 'expired', rails70_cache_payload('stale', :expires_at => 1.minute.ago.to_f)
    assert_nil @store.read('expired')
    assert_not @store.exist?('expired')
  end

  # A memcache store of Rails 6.1 uses NullCoder (Dalli unmarshals the
  # payload) and would otherwise return the binary payload as the value.
  def test_rails70_payload_from_a_store_without_coder_is_read
    skip 'Rails 7.0 reads its own format' if rails70?

    store = ActiveSupport::Cache::FileStore.new(@cache_dir, :coder => nil)
    entry = store.send(:deserialize_entry, rails70_cache_payload('formatted text', :version => 'v1'))
    assert_kind_of ActiveSupport::Cache::Entry, entry
    assert_equal 'formatted text', entry.value
    assert_equal 'v1', entry.version

    # raw values are left alone
    assert_equal "\x00raw".b, store.send(:deserialize_entry, "\x00raw".b)
    assert_equal '42', store.send(:deserialize_entry, '42')
  end

  def test_cache_entries_are_written_in_the_rails61_format
    skip 'Rails 7.0 on its defaults writes the 7.0 format' if rails70?

    # the format of the previous release, which Rails 7.0 reads too
    @store.write('key', 'value', :expires_in => 1.hour)
    payload = File.binread(cache_file('key'))
    assert payload.start_with?("\x04\x08".b)
    entry = Marshal.load(payload) # rubocop:disable Security/MarshalLoad
    assert_kind_of ActiveSupport::Cache::Entry, entry
    assert_equal 'value', entry.value
  end

  def test_key_generators_match_the_rails_key_generators
    secret = Rails.application.secret_key_base
    sha1, sha256 = RedmineApp::ReleaseCompatibility.key_generators(secret)
    assert_equal OpenSSL::Digest::SHA1, sha1.digest
    assert_equal OpenSSL::Digest::SHA256, sha256.digest

    # Rails 6.1 derives with SHA1, Rails 7.0 on its defaults with SHA256
    expected = rails70? ? sha256 : sha1
    assert_equal Rails.application.key_generator.generate_key('salt', 32), expected.generate_key('salt', 32)
    assert_equal OpenSSL::PKCS5.pbkdf2_hmac_sha1(secret, 'salt', 1000, 64), sha1.generate_key('salt')
    assert_not_equal sha1.generate_key('salt'), sha256.generate_key('salt')
  end

  def test_message_verifier_verifies_messages_signed_by_either_release
    data = {'user_id' => 3, 'issue_id' => 2}
    RedmineApp::ReleaseCompatibility.key_generators(Rails.application.secret_key_base).each do |generator|
      token = ActiveSupport::MessageVerifier.new(generator.generate_key('mail_links')).generate(data, :purpose => :unwatch)
      assert_equal data, Rails.application.message_verifier(:mail_links).verify(token, :purpose => :unwatch)
    end
    assert_raise ActiveSupport::MessageVerifier::InvalidSignature do
      Rails.application.message_verifier(:mail_links).verify('garbage--0123', :purpose => :unwatch)
    end
  end
end

steps.reasoning_content:
I'm tracing how `store` builds its accessors internally, noting that in Rails 7.2 it wraps the serializer construction with `build_column_serializer` before passing an `IndifferentCoder` into `serialize`.

My shim needs to handle the 7.0 internal path where `store` calls `serialize` positionally with the coder, so that call still passes through correctly. Since there's no `application_record.rb`, models inherit directly from `ActiveRecord::Base`, so I'll place the shim in the patches file and update the relevant call sites.

arguments.command:

shim = <<~R
  # Models call serialize with the keywords of Rails 7.1+ (coder:, type:),
  # Rails 7.0 only takes a positional class or coder. Same column format.
  # TODO: remove with Rails 7.0 (see docs/UPGRADE.md)
  if ActiveRecord.gem_version < Gem::Version.new(%q(7.1))
    module AttributeMethods
      module Serialization
        module ClassMethods
          alias_method :serialize_without_coder_keyword, :serialize
          def serialize(attr_name, class_name_or_coder = Object, coder: nil, type: Object, **options)

            end

        end
      end
    end

# frozen_string_literal: true

# Compatibility between adjacent releases of the Rails upgrade
# (Rails 6.1 -> 7.0 -> 7.2, see docs/UPGRADE.md).
#
# Every release must be able to read what the release before it and the
# release after it write, so that neither a deploy nor a rollback signs anyone
# out or breaks a link in a mail that was already sent:
#
# * session cookies (encrypted cookie jar) and signed cookies,
# * links signed with Rails.application.message_verifier (Mailer.mail_link_token),
# * CSRF tokens of the forms already rendered in browsers,
# * entries of a cache store shared between releases.
#
# This file is loaded both on Rails 7.0 (Gemfile, production) and on Rails 7.2
# with its framework defaults (Gemfile.next, next release). It never changes
# the format written by the running release, it only lets it read the other
# formats. See docs/UPGRADE.md for the details and for when each part can go.
module RedmineApp
  module ReleaseCompatibility
    # Rails 7.1 changed the formats of signed messages, cache entries and
    # marshalled records (see below). Rails 7.1+ reads the Rails 7.0 formats
    # natively, Rails 7.0 needs the readers defined at the end of this file.
    READS_RAILS71_FORMATS = ActiveSupport.gem_version >= Gem::Version.new('7.1')

    # Rails derives the secrets of cookies and message verifiers from
    # secret_key_base with PBKDF2 (1000 iterations, see
    # Rails::Application#key_generator). Rails 6.1 on legacy defaults hashes
    # with SHA1, Rails 7.0+ on its defaults with SHA256
    # (config.active_support.key_generator_hash_digest_class).
    KEY_DERIVATION_DIGESTS = [OpenSSL::Digest::SHA1, OpenSSL::Digest::SHA256].freeze
    KEY_DERIVATION_ITERATIONS = 1000

    # Same keys as ActiveSupport::KeyGenerator, with an explicit digest.
    class KeyGenerator
      attr_reader :digest

      def initialize(secret, digest)
        @secret = secret
        @digest = digest
        @keys = Concurrent::Map.new
      end

      def generate_key(salt, key_size=64)
        @keys.compute_if_absent([salt, key_size]) do
          OpenSSL::PKCS5.pbkdf2_hmac(@secret, salt, KEY_DERIVATION_ITERATIONS, key_size, @digest.new)
        end
      end
    end

    class << self
      def key_generators(secret)
        KEY_DERIVATION_DIGESTS.map {|digest| KeyGenerator.new(secret, digest)}
      end

      # Adds rotations to the cookie jars for the cookie formats written by
      # the releases of the upgrade:
      # * Rails 6.1 on legacy defaults: AES-256-CBC + HMAC, SHA1 derived keys
      # * Rails 7.0 and 7.2 on their defaults: AES-256-GCM, SHA256 derived keys
      # (the cookie payload is JSON with the Rails 7.0 purpose metadata in all
      # of them, Rails 7.2 keeps it for cookies). Rails decrypts with the
      # format of the running release first and rewrites a cookie read with a
      # rotation in that format.
      def add_cookie_rotations(config, key_generators)
        rotations = config.cookies_rotations
        gcm, cbc = 'aes-256-gcm', 'aes-256-cbc'
        key_generators.each do |generator|
          rotations.rotate(
            :encrypted,
            generator.generate_key(
              config.authenticated_encrypted_cookie_salt,
              ActiveSupport::MessageEncryptor.key_len(gcm)
            ),
            nil,
            :cipher => gcm
          )
          rotations.rotate(
            :encrypted,
            generator.generate_key(config.encrypted_cookie_salt, ActiveSupport::MessageEncryptor.key_len(cbc)),
            generator.generate_key(config.encrypted_signed_cookie_salt),
            :cipher => cbc,
            :digest => config.cookies_digest || 'SHA1'
          )
          rotations.rotate(
            :signed,
            generator.generate_key(config.signed_cookie_salt),
            :digest => config.signed_cookie_digest || 'SHA1'
          )
        end
        rotations
      end

      # Lets a message verifier verify messages signed by any release.
      def add_verifier_rotations(verifier, verifier_name, key_generators)
        key_generators.each do |generator|
          verifier.rotate(generator.generate_key(verifier_name.to_s))
        end
        verifier
      end
    end

    # Rails.application.message_verifier(name) signs with the key derivation
    # of the running release and verifies with both. Used for the links in
    # mails (Mailer.mail_link_token), which are valid for 30 days.
    module MessageVerifiers
      def message_verifier(verifier_name)
        @release_compatibility_verifiers ||= Concurrent::Map.new
        @release_compatibility_verifiers.compute_if_absent(verifier_name) do
          verifier =
            if READS_RAILS71_FORMATS
              super(verifier_name)
            else
              # What Rails 7.0 builds (same secret, digest and serializer, so
              # it signs alike), able to read Rails 7.1+ messages too.
              Rails71MessageVerifier.new(key_generator.generate_key(verifier_name.to_s))
            end
          ReleaseCompatibility.add_verifier_rotations(
            verifier, verifier_name, ReleaseCompatibility.key_generators(secret_key_base)
          )
        end
      end
    end

    unless READS_RAILS71_FORMATS
      # Rails 7.1+ on its defaults (message_serializer :json_allow_marshal,
      # use_message_serializer_for_metadata) signs JSON messages and puts the
      # metadata in the serialized envelope:
      #   {"_rails":{"data":<value>,"exp":"<ISO 8601>","pur":"<purpose>"}}
      # Rails 7.0 only knows its own envelope ({"_rails":{"message":<base64>}})
      # and raises a NoMethodError (an error page) on the new one. This
      # verifier verifies both, with the same purpose and expiry checks. It
      # signs like Rails 7.0 (Marshal, Rails 7.0 envelope), which Rails 6.1 and
      # Rails 7.1+ read. Its rotations are instances of this class too.
      class Rails71MessageVerifier < ActiveSupport::MessageVerifier
        MARSHAL_SIGNATURE = "\x04\x08".b.freeze
        RAILS70_ENVELOPE = '{"_rails":{"message":'

        def verified(signed_message, purpose: nil, **options)
          message = rails71_message(signed_message)
          return super if message.nil?

          read_rails71_message(message, purpose)
        end

        private

        # The message, if it is signed with the secret of this verifier and
        # is not in a format Rails 7.0 reads itself.
        def rails71_message(signed_message)
          data, digest = get_data_and_digest_from(signed_message)
          return unless digest_matches_data?(digest, data)

          message = decode(data)
          message unless message.start_with?(MARSHAL_SIGNATURE, RAILS70_ENVELOPE)
        rescue ArgumentError # invalid base64
          nil
        end

        def read_rails71_message(message, purpose)
          value = ActiveSupport::JSON.decode(message)
          if value.is_a?(Hash) && value.key?('_rails')
            metadata = value['_rails']
            return unless metadata.is_a?(Hash) && metadata['pur'].to_s == purpose.to_s
            return if metadata['exp'] && Time.now.utc >= parse_expiry(metadata['exp'])

            metadata['data']
          elsif purpose.nil?
            # message without metadata
            value
          end
        rescue JSON::ParserError, ArgumentError, TypeError
          nil
        end

        def parse_expiry(expiry)
          ActiveSupport.use_standard_json_time_format ? Time.iso8601(expiry) : Time.parse(expiry)
        end
      end

      # Rails 7.1+ on its defaults writes cache entries in the 7.1 format
      # (config.active_support.cache_format_version = 7.1) which Rails 7.0
      # cannot read: a file store raises a TypeError (an error page wherever
      # the entry is used, eg. formatted wiki text), the other stores log an
      # error and miss. Rails 7.0 keeps writing the 7.0 format, which Rails
      # 7.1+ reads. 7.1 entries start with "\x00\x11", which no 7.0 entry
      # ("\x00\x04\x08", "\x01" + deflated data) nor 6.1 entry ("\x04\x08")
      # does. Only applies to the default coder of a store.
      module Rails71CacheEntries
        SIGNATURE = "\x00\x11".b.freeze
        # type, expires_at (-1.0: none), version length (-1: none)
        HEADER_TEMPLATE = 'CEl<'
        HEADER_SIZE = SIGNATURE.bytesize + [0, 0.0, 0].pack(HEADER_TEMPLATE).bytesize
        OBJECT_DUMP_TYPE = 0x01
        STRING_ENCODINGS = {0x02 => Encoding::UTF_8, 0x03 => Encoding::BINARY, 0x04 => Encoding::US_ASCII}.freeze
        COMPRESSED_FLAG = 0x80
        MARSHAL_SIGNATURE = "\x04\x08".b.freeze

        private

        def deserialize_entry(payload, **options)
          if payload.is_a?(String) && payload.start_with?(SIGNATURE) && @coder.equal?(default_coder)
            load_rails71_entry(payload)
          else
            super
          end
        end

        # ActiveSupport::Cache::Coder#dump of Rails 7.1+, with its default
        # (Marshal) serializer and Zlib compressor
        def load_rails71_entry(payload)
          type, expires_at, version_length = payload.unpack("@#{SIGNATURE.bytesize}#{HEADER_TEMPLATE}")
          version = payload.byteslice(HEADER_SIZE, version_length) if version_length >= 0
          data = payload.byteslice((HEADER_SIZE + [version_length, 0].max)..-1)
          data = Zlib::Inflate.inflate(data) if type & COMPRESSED_FLAG > 0
          type &= ~COMPRESSED_FLAG

          value =
            if (encoding = STRING_ENCODINGS[type])
              data.force_encoding(encoding)
            elsif type == OBJECT_DUMP_TYPE && data.start_with?(MARSHAL_SIGNATURE)
              # unmarshalled like Rails itself does for its cache entries
              Marshal.load(data) # rubocop:disable Security/MarshalLoad
            else
              return nil
            end
          if version&.start_with?(MARSHAL_SIGNATURE)
            version = Marshal.load(version) # rubocop:disable Security/MarshalLoad
          else
            version&.force_encoding(Encoding::UTF_8)
          end

          ActiveSupport::Cache::Entry.new(value, :version => version, :expires_at => (expires_at if expires_at >= 0))
        rescue Zlib::Error, TypeError, ArgumentError, NameError
          nil
        end
      end

      # Rails 7.1+ on its defaults (active_record.marshalling_format_version
      # 7.1) marshals records with marshal_dump, which Rails 7.0 cannot load
      # (TypeError, eg. for records in a cache entry). Backport of
      # ActiveRecord::Marshalling::Methods#marshal_load of Rails 7.1, for
      # loading only: Rails 7.0 keeps marshalling records in its own format.
      module Rails71MarshalledRecords
        def marshal_load(state)
          attributes_from_database, new_record, associations = state

          attributes = self.class.attributes_builder.build_from_database(attributes_from_database)
          init_with_attributes(attributes, new_record)

          associations&.each do |name, target|
            association(name).target = target
          rescue ActiveRecord::AssociationNotFoundError
            # the association no longer exists
          end
        end
      end
    end
  end
end

Rails::Application.prepend RedmineApp::ReleaseCompatibility::MessageVerifiers

unless RedmineApp::ReleaseCompatibility::READS_RAILS71_FORMATS
  require 'active_support/cache'
  ActiveSupport::Cache::Store.prepend RedmineApp::ReleaseCompatibility::Rails71CacheEntries

  ActiveSupport.on_load(:active_record) do
    include RedmineApp::ReleaseCompatibility::Rails71MarshalledRecords
  end
end

# secret_key_base is set by config/initializers/secret_token.rb, which is
# loaded after this file.
Rails.application.config.after_initialize do |app|
  secret =
    begin
      app.secret_key_base

    RedmineApp::ReleaseCompatibility.add_cookie_rotations(
      app.config.action_dispatch, RedmineApp::ReleaseCompatibility.key_generators(secret)
    )
  end
end

I'm deciding to skip adding an explicit test asserting that Marshal-based R0 session cookies get rejected on R2, since that documents an intentional ship-gate limitation better suited for docs than for an assertion. Now I'm mapping out the write-side cross-compatibility tests: verifying 7.0-written session cookies decrypt correctly under both R1 and R3 (since 7.2 natively reads 7.0 envelopes), confirming 7.2-written cookies match the 7.0 format so R2 can read them, and checking that mail link tokens written on 7.0 use Marshal with a SHA256 envelope.

I'm also setting up a check that Rails 7.0's message_verifier signs identically to the native verifier, confirming R1's verifier correctly rotates between SHA1 and SHA256 keys, then moving into writing unit tests for the cache builders.

Instead, I'm considering manually assembling the raw Marshal byte stream: prepend the header and type byte, encode the class name as a symbol with its length-prefixed string, then append the dumped state bytes with the header stripped off. The tricky part is that Marshal's internal symbol and object link tables index by position, so concatenating pieces this way risks breaking those references.

However, I realize that nested attributes like Time objects carry instance variables that get marshaled as symbols (`:offset`, `:zone`), which would introduce their own symlink entries and conflict with the indices from the prepended class symbol — making this hand-rolled approach fragile. A safer route might be to define a `marshal_dump` method on the class itself rather than trying to splice raw bytes.

Actually since 7.2 bundle already defaults to loading 7.2, real Marshal.dump there would use the 7.1 format natively, so I could validate my simulated 7.0 dump by comparing byte output against the genuine 7.1 dump on 7.2 — if attributes_for_database values match, the bytes should be identical. # frozen_string_literal: true

require_relative '../test_helper'

# Adjacent releases of the Rails upgrade must read what each other write, so
# that neither a deploy nor a rollback signs anyone out or breaks a link in a
# mail already sent (see docs/UPGRADE.md and
# config/initializers/15-release_compatibility.rb).
#
# The cookies and tokens of the releases are built here from scratch, with
# the key derivation, cipher, serializer and metadata each release uses:
# * Rails 6.1 on legacy defaults (previous release): PBKDF2-SHA1 keys,
#   AES-256-CBC + HMAC cookies with a JSON payload and no metadata, global
#   CSRF tokens (standard base64), Marshal mail link tokens with the Rails
#   7.0 metadata envelope.
# * Rails 7.0 on its defaults (this release): PBKDF2-SHA256 keys,
#   AES-256-GCM cookies with a JSON payload in the Rails 7.0 metadata
#   envelope, per-form CSRF tokens, Marshal mail link tokens with the Rails
#   7.0 metadata envelope.
# * Rails 7.2 on its defaults (next release): cookies and CSRF tokens as
#   Rails 7.0, JSON mail link tokens with the metadata in the serialized
#   envelope (Rails 7.1 format).
#
# Runs on Rails 7.0 (Gemfile) and on Rails 7.2 (Gemfile.next). The tests of
# what the running release writes check that it is exactly what the builders
# below build, so the tests run on the other bundle exercise the real format.
class ReleaseCompatibilityTest < Redmine::IntegrationTest
  fixtures :projects, :users, :email_addresses, :roles, :members, :member_roles,
           :trackers, :projects_trackers, :enabled_modules, :issue_statuses, :issues,
           :enumerations, :custom_fields, :custom_values, :custom_fields_trackers,
           :watchers, :user_preferences

  SESSION_COOKIE = '_redmine_session'
  NULL_SERIALIZER = ActiveSupport::MessageEncryptor::NullSerializer
  SHA1 = OpenSSL::Digest::SHA1
  SHA256 = OpenSSL::Digest::SHA256
  MAIL_LINK_DATA = {'user_id' => 3, 'issue_id' => 2}.freeze

  def rails72?
    Rails.gem_version >= Gem::Version.new('7.2')
  end

  def derive_key(salt, digest, key_size=64)
    OpenSSL::PKCS5.pbkdf2_hmac(Rails.application.secret_key_base, salt, 1000, key_size, digest.new)
  end

  # Rails 7.0 metadata envelope, also used by Rails 6.1 for messages and by
  # Rails 7.2 for cookies
  def rails70_envelope(serialized, purpose:, expires_at: nil)
    ActiveSupport::JSON.encode(
      '_rails' => {
        'message' => Base64.strict_encode64(serialized),
        'exp' => expires_at&.utc&.iso8601(3),
        'pur' => purpose
      }
    )
  end

  # Encrypted cookie jar of Rails 7.0 and Rails 7.2 on their defaults
  def gcm_encryptor
    ActiveSupport::MessageEncryptor.new(
      derive_key('authenticated encrypted cookie', SHA256, 32),
      :cipher => 'aes-256-gcm', :serializer => NULL_SERIALIZER
    )
  end

  # Encrypted cookie jar of Rails 6.1 on legacy defaults
  def cbc_encryptor
    ActiveSupport::MessageEncryptor.new(
      derive_key('encrypted cookie', SHA1, 32),
      derive_key('signed encrypted cookie', SHA1),
      :cipher => 'aes-256-cbc', :serializer => NULL_SERIALIZER
    )
  end

  # Session cookie written by this release and by the next one
  def rails70_session_cookie(data)
    gcm_encryptor.encrypt_and_sign(
      rails70_envelope(ActiveSupport::JSON.encode(data), :purpose => "cookie.#{SESSION_COOKIE}")
    )
  end

  # Session cookie written by the previous release (JSON, it ran with the
  # :hybrid cookie serializer)
  def rails61_session_cookie(data)
    cbc_encryptor.encrypt_and_sign(ActiveSupport::JSON.encode(data))
  end

  def session_data(user, data={})
    {
      'session_id' => SecureRandom.hex(16),
      'user_id' => user.id,
      'tk' => user.generate_session_token,
      '_csrf_token' => SecureRandom.urlsafe_base64(32)
    }.merge(data)
  end

  # Rack::Test (un)escapes cookie values itself
  def set_session_cookie(value)
    cookies[SESSION_COOKIE] = value
  end

  # The session cookie written by the running release, which must be the
  # format of rails70_session_cookie on both Rails 7.0 and Rails 7.2: the
  # previous release reads it (AES-256-GCM, SHA256 keys and the Rails 7.0
  # metadata, see its own tests) and so do Rails 7.0 and Rails 7.2.
  def decrypt_written_session_cookie
    value = cookies[SESSION_COOKIE]
    assert value, 'no session cookie was written'
    envelope = ActiveSupport::JSON.decode(gcm_encryptor.decrypt_and_verify(value))
    assert_equal ['_rails'], envelope.keys
    assert_equal "cookie.#{SESSION_COOKIE}", envelope['_rails']['pur']
    assert_nil envelope['_rails']['exp']
    ActiveSupport::JSON.decode(Base64.strict_decode64(envelope['_rails']['message']))
  end

  def assert_signed_in_as(login)
    get '/my/account'
    assert_response :success
    assert_select '#loggedas a', :text => login
  end

  def with_redmine_session_verification
    saved = Rails.application.config.redmine_verify_sessions
    Rails.application.config.redmine_verify_sessions = true
    yield
  ensure
    Rails.application.config.redmine_verify_sessions = saved
  end

  def with_forgery_protection
    saved = ActionController::Base.allow_forgery_protection
    ActionController::Base.allow_forgery_protection = true
    yield
  ensure
    ActionController::Base.allow_forgery_protection = saved
  end

  # Sessions

  def test_session_written_by_rails70_or_rails72_on_their_defaults_is_accepted
    with_redmine_session_verification do
      set_session_cookie rails70_session_cookie(session_data(User.find(2)))
      assert_signed_in_as 'jsmith'
      assert_equal 2, decrypt_written_session_cookie['user_id']
    end
  end

  def test_session_written_by_the_previous_release_is_accepted_and_rewritten
    with_redmine_session_verification do
      set_session_cookie rails61_session_cookie(session_data(User.find(2)))
      assert_signed_in_as 'jsmith'
      # rewritten in the format of the running release
      assert_equal 2, decrypt_written_session_cookie['user_id']
    end
  end

  def test_session_written_on_login_can_be_read_by_the_adjacent_releases
    log_user('jsmith', 'jsmith')
    data = decrypt_written_session_cookie
    assert_equal 2, data['user_id']
    assert data['tk'].present?
  end

  def test_tampered_session_is_rejected
    with_redmine_session_verification do
      value = rails70_session_cookie(session_data(User.find(2)))
      set_session_cookie value.sub(/\A./) {|c| c == 'A' ? 'B' : 'A'}
      get '/my/account'
      assert_response :redirect
    end
  end

  def test_issue_query_from_a_json_session_is_restored
    query = {
      'project_id' => 1,
      'filters' => {'status_id' => {'operator' => 'c', 'values' => ['']}},
      'group_by' => 'tracker',
      'column_names' => ['tracker', 'subject'],
      'totalable_names' => [],
      'sort' => [['id', 'asc']]
    }
    set_session_cookie rails70_session_cookie(session_data(User.find(2), 'issue_query' => query))

    get '/projects/ecookbook/issues'
    assert_response :success
    assert_select 'tr.issue', :minimum => 1
    assert_select 'tr.issue:not(.closed)', 0
    assert_select 'tr.group', :minimum => 1
    assert_select 'table.issues thead th.subject'
    assert_select 'table.issues thead th.status', 0
  end

  def test_saved_issue_query_from_a_json_session_is_restored
    set_session_cookie rails70_session_cookie(
      session_data(User.find(2), 'issue_query' => {'id' => 1, 'project_id' => 1})
    )

    get '/projects/ecookbook/issues'
    assert_response :success
    assert_select 'h2', :text => IssueQuery.find(1).name
  end

  # CSRF tokens of forms rendered in browsers

  def xor_byte_strings(s1, s2)
    s1.bytes.zip(s2.bytes).map {|a, b| a ^ b}.pack('C*')
  end

  def masked_token(raw_token, encoding=:urlsafe)
    one_time_pad = SecureRandom.random_bytes(raw_token.bytesize)
    masked = one_time_pad + xor_byte_strings(one_time_pad, raw_token)
    encoding == :urlsafe ? Base64.urlsafe_encode64(masked, :padding => false) : Base64.strict_encode64(masked)
  end

  def unmasked_token(token)
    masked = Base64.urlsafe_decode64(token)
    xor_byte_strings(masked[0, 32], masked[32..-1])
  end

  def real_csrf_token
    Base64.urlsafe_decode64(session[:_csrf_token])
  end

  # Per-form token as rendered by Rails 7.0 and Rails 7.2 on their defaults
  def per_form_csrf_token(action, method, real_token=real_csrf_token)
    OpenSSL::HMAC.digest(SHA256.new, real_token, "#{action}##{method}")
  end

  # Global token as rendered by Rails 6.1 on legacy defaults
  def global_csrf_token(real_token)
    OpenSSL::HMAC.digest(SHA256.new, real_token, '!real_csrf_token')
  end

  def test_form_rendered_with_a_per_form_token_is_accepted
    log_user('jsmith', 'jsmith')
    with_forgery_protection do
      get '/my/account'
      put '/my/account', :params => {
        :user => {:firstname => 'Johnny'},
        :authenticity_token => masked_token(per_form_csrf_token('/my/account', 'put'))
      }
      assert_redirected_to '/my/account'
      assert_equal 'Johnny', User.find(2).firstname
      assert_signed_in_as 'jsmith'
    end
  end

  def test_per_form_token_for_another_form_is_rejected
    log_user('jsmith', 'jsmith')
    with_forgery_protection do
      get '/my/account'
      put '/my/account', :params => {
        :user => {:firstname => 'Johnny'},
        :authenticity_token => masked_token(per_form_csrf_token('/my/password', 'post'))
      }
      assert_response 422
      assert_equal 'John', User.find(2).firstname
    end
  end

  def test_form_rendered_by_the_previous_release_is_accepted
    # Rails 6.1 on legacy defaults stores the CSRF token in standard base64
    # and renders global tokens in standard base64
    encoded = SecureRandom.base64(32) until encoded&.match?(/[+\/]/)
    real_token = Base64.strict_decode64(encoded)
    with_redmine_session_verification do
      set_session_cookie rails61_session_cookie(session_data(User.find(2), '_csrf_token' => encoded))
      with_forgery_protection do
        put '/my/account', :params => {
          :user => {:firstname => 'Johnny'},
          :authenticity_token => masked_token(global_csrf_token(real_token), :strict)
        }
        assert_redirected_to '/my/account'
      end
      assert_equal 'Johnny', User.find(2).firstname
      assert_signed_in_as 'jsmith'
    end
  end

  def test_forms_rendered_by_this_release_have_per_form_tokens
    # the previous release accepts per-form tokens (see its own tests) and
    # Rails 7.0 and Rails 7.2 accept them natively
    log_user('jsmith', 'jsmith')
    token = with_forgery_protection do
      get '/my/account'
      css_select('form[action="/my/account"] input[name=authenticity_token]').first['value']
    end
    assert_equal per_form_csrf_token('/my/account', 'post'), unmasked_token(token)
  end

  # Links in mails

  # Mail link token as signed by Rails 6.1 on legacy defaults (SHA1 key) and
  # by Rails 7.0 on its defaults (SHA256 key)
  def rails70_mail_link_token(digest, data: MAIL_LINK_DATA, purpose: 'unwatch', expires_at: 30.days.from_now)
    sign_message(
      derive_key('mail_links', digest),
      rails70_envelope(Marshal.dump(data), :purpose => purpose, :expires_at => expires_at)
    )
  end

  # Mail link token as signed by Rails 7.2 on its defaults (SHA256 key)
  def rails71_mail_link_token(data: MAIL_LINK_DATA, purpose: 'unwatch', expires_at: 30.days.from_now)
    sign_message(
      derive_key('mail_links', SHA256),
      ActiveSupport::JSON.encode(
        '_rails' => {'data' => data, 'exp' => expires_at.utc.iso8601(3), 'pur' => purpose}
      )
    )
  end

  def sign_message(secret, message)
    data = Base64.strict_encode64(message)
    "#{data}--#{OpenSSL::HMAC.hexdigest('SHA1', secret, data)}"
  end

  def assert_unwatch_link_works(token)
    assert Issue.find(2).watched_by?(User.find(3))
    get '/mail_links/unwatch', :params => {:token => token}
    assert_response :success
    assert_not Issue.find(2).watched_by?(User.find(3))
  end

  def assert_unwatch_link_rejected(token)
    get '/mail_links/unwatch', :params => {:token => token}
    assert_response 404
    assert Issue.find(2).watched_by?(User.find(3))
  end

  def test_mail_link_sent_by_the_previous_release_works
    assert_unwatch_link_works rails70_mail_link_token(SHA1)
  end

  def test_mail_link_sent_by_rails70_on_its_defaults_works
    assert_unwatch_link_works rails70_mail_link_token(SHA256)
  end

  def test_mail_link_sent_by_rails72_on_its_defaults_works
    assert_unwatch_link_works rails71_mail_link_token
  end

  def test_mail_link_with_another_purpose_is_rejected
    assert_unwatch_link_rejected rails70_mail_link_token(SHA256, :purpose => 'other')
    assert_unwatch_link_rejected rails71_mail_link_token(:purpose => 'other')
  end

  def test_expired_mail_link_is_rejected
    assert_unwatch_link_rejected rails70_mail_link_token(SHA1, :expires_at => 1.minute.ago)
    assert_unwatch_link_rejected rails71_mail_link_token(:expires_at => 1.minute.ago)
  end

  def test_mail_link_with_an_invalid_signature_is_rejected
    token = rails71_mail_link_token
    assert_unwatch_link_rejected token.sub(/[0-9a-f]\z/) {|c| c == '0' ? '1' : '0'}
    assert_unwatch_link_rejected sign_message('another secret', Base64.strict_decode64(token.split('--').first))
  end

  def test_mail_link_sent_by_this_release_works_on_the_adjacent_releases
    travel_to Time.zone.parse('2026-01-15 12:00:00') do
      token = Mailer.mail_link_token(:unwatch, MAIL_LINK_DATA)
      if rails72?
        # read by Rails 7.0 thanks to the compatibility code (see
        # test_mail_link_sent_by_rails72_on_its_defaults_works on Rails 7.0)
        assert_equal rails71_mail_link_token, token
      else
        # read by Rails 6.1 (with its SHA256 rotation) and by Rails 7.2
        assert_equal rails70_mail_link_token(SHA256), token
      end
      assert_unwatch_link_works token
    end
  end
end

I'm realizing the decrypt failure means the metadata envelope gets wrapped before encryption in Rails 7.0, so my plain GCM encryptor without the purpose context can't properly decode the wrapped plaintext.

Better to bypass Rails' metadata handling entirely and do raw AES-256-GCM decryption/encryption manually with OpenSSL, parsing the base64 segments for ciphertext, iv, and auth tag myself. Writing raw GCM helper functions...

The CBC value gets signed with MessageVerifier using a SHA1 HMAC to produce the final cookie string. For both CBC and GCM writes, using MessageEncryptor with NullSerializer and no purpose works fine across Rails 7.0 and 7.2 since there's no metadata wrapping to worry about—the plaintext passes through as-is. The real issue only shows up on decryption.

For reliability, I should use raw OpenSSL for the GCM decrypt helper rather than relying on ActiveSupport's envelope interpretation. Now I'm turning to the per-form token mismatch test—checking how Rails computes tokens for a form rendered with `form_for @user, url: my_account_path, method: :put`, since Rails actually renders method="post" with a hidden `_method=put` field, and the per-form token calculation needs to account for that method substitution.

So the method used for action is the original one, which here should be "put" not "post" since the account form likely uses put for updates. I need to adjust my test to use 'put' as the method in the per_form_csrf_token call and verify this matches the actual form being targeted.

I found two test issues: Rails 7.0's `MessageEncryptor` always processes the metadata envelope on decrypt, so I'll decrypt AES-GCM directly with OpenSSL to inspect raw plaintext, and the account form actually uses `put` rather than `post`. Fixing both now.

# frozen_string_literal: true

require_relative '../test_helper'

# See config/initializers/15-release_compatibility.rb and docs/UPGRADE.md.
# Runs on Rails 7.0 (Gemfile) and on Rails 7.2 (Gemfile.next). The cache
# entries of each release are built from scratch; the tests of what the
# running release writes check that it is exactly what the builders build.
class ReleaseCompatibilityKeysAndCacheTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  fixtures :projects, :users, :trackers, :issue_statuses, :enumerations, :issues

  def setup
    @cache_dir = Dir.mktmpdir
    @store = ActiveSupport::Cache::FileStore.new(@cache_dir)
  end

  def teardown
    FileUtils.rm_rf(@cache_dir)
  end

  def rails72?
    Rails.gem_version >= Gem::Version.new('7.2')
  end

  def cache_file(key)
    @store.send(:normalize_key, key, {})
  end

  def write_cache_payload(key, payload)
    path = cache_file(key)
    FileUtils.mkdir_p(File.dirname(path))
    File.binwrite(path, payload)
  end

  # Cache payload written by Rails 6.1 on legacy defaults (previous release)
  def rails61_cache_payload(value, expires_in: nil, version: nil)
    Marshal.dump(ActiveSupport::Cache::Entry.new(value, :expires_in => expires_in, :version => version))
  end

  # Cache payload written by Rails 7.0 on its defaults (this release)
  def rails70_cache_payload(value, expires_at: nil, version: nil, compress: false)
    members = [value, expires_at, version]
    members.pop while !members.empty? && members.last.nil?
    payload = Marshal.dump(members)
    compress ? "\x01".b + Zlib::Deflate.deflate(payload) : "\x00".b + payload
  end

  # Cache payload written by Rails 7.2 on its defaults (next release,
  # cache_format_version 7.1)
  def rails71_cache_payload(value, expires_at: nil, version: nil, compress: false)
    type, data =
      if value.instance_of?(String)
        [{Encoding::UTF_8 => 0x02, Encoding::BINARY => 0x03, Encoding::US_ASCII => 0x04}.fetch(value.encoding), value.b]
      else
        [0x01, Marshal.dump(value)]
      end
    if compress
      type |= 0x80
      data = Zlib::Deflate.deflate(data)
    end
    version = version&.b
    "\x00\x11".b + [type, expires_at || -1.0, version ? version.bytesize : -1].pack('CEl<') + version.to_s + data
  end

  def test_cache_entries_written_by_any_release_are_read
    {
      'rails61' => method(:rails61_cache_payload),
      'rails70' => method(:rails70_cache_payload),
      'rails71' => method(:rails71_cache_payload)
    }.each do |format, builder|
      write_cache_payload "#{format}/plain", builder.call('formatted text')
      write_cache_payload "#{format}/object", builder.call([%w(a b), {'c' => 1}])
      write_cache_payload "#{format}/versioned", builder.call('value', :version => 'v1')

      assert_equal 'formatted text', @store.read("#{format}/plain"), format
      assert_equal [%w(a b), {'c' => 1}], @store.read("#{format}/object"), format
      assert_equal 'value', @store.read("#{format}/versioned", :version => 'v1'), format
      assert_nil @store.read("#{format}/versioned", :version => 'v2'), format
    end
  end

  def test_compressed_cache_entries_written_by_rails70_and_rails72_are_read
    text = 'x' * 5000
    write_cache_payload 'rails70', rails70_cache_payload(text, :compress => true)
    write_cache_payload 'rails71', rails71_cache_payload(text, :compress => true)
    write_cache_payload 'rails71/object', rails71_cache_payload([text], :compress => true)

    assert_equal text, @store.read('rails70')
    assert_equal text, @store.read('rails71')
    assert_equal Encoding::UTF_8, @store.read('rails71').encoding
    assert_equal [text], @store.read('rails71/object')
  end

  def test_expired_cache_entries_written_by_rails70_and_rails72_are_ignored
    write_cache_payload 'rails70', rails70_cache_payload('stale', :expires_at => 1.minute.ago.to_f)
    write_cache_payload 'rails71', rails71_cache_payload('stale', :expires_at => 1.minute.ago.to_f)
    write_cache_payload 'rails71/fresh', rails71_cache_payload('fresh', :expires_at => 1.minute.from_now.to_f)

    assert_nil @store.read('rails70')
    assert_nil @store.read('rails71')
    assert_not @store.exist?('rails71')
    assert_equal 'fresh', @store.read('rails71/fresh')
  end

  def test_invalid_rails71_cache_entry_is_a_miss
    write_cache_payload 'truncated', rails71_cache_payload([1, 2], :compress => true)[0..-4]
    assert_nil @store.read('truncated')
    assert_equal 'computed', @store.fetch('truncated') {'computed'}
  end

  # A memcache store reads the payload through Dalli, which unmarshals it.
  def test_rails71_payload_from_a_mem_cache_store_is_read
    require 'dalli'
  rescue LoadError
    skip 'dalli is not installed'
  else
    store = ActiveSupport::Cache::MemCacheStore.new
    entry = store.send(:deserialize_entry, rails71_cache_payload('formatted text', :version => 'v1'))
    assert_kind_of ActiveSupport::Cache::Entry, entry
    assert_equal 'formatted text', entry.value
    assert_equal 'v1', entry.version
  end

  def test_cache_entries_written_by_this_release_have_the_expected_format
    text = 'x' * 5000
    @store.write('plain', 'formatted text')
    @store.write('object', %w(a b), :version => 'v1')
    @store.write('compressed', text)
    if rails72?
      # Rails 7.1 format, read by Rails 7.0 thanks to the compatibility code
      assert_equal rails71_cache_payload('formatted text'), File.binread(cache_file('plain'))
      assert_equal rails71_cache_payload(%w(a b), :version => 'v1'), File.binread(cache_file('object'))
      assert_equal rails71_cache_payload(text, :compress => true), File.binread(cache_file('compressed'))
    else
      # Rails 7.0 format, read by Rails 6.1 (see its own tests) and Rails 7.2
      assert_equal rails70_cache_payload('formatted text'), File.binread(cache_file('plain'))
      assert_equal rails70_cache_payload(%w(a b), :version => 'v1'), File.binread(cache_file('object'))
      assert_equal rails70_cache_payload(text, :compress => true), File.binread(cache_file('compressed'))
    end
  end

  # Records marshalled by Rails 7.2 on its defaults
  # (active_record.marshalling_format_version 7.1), eg. in a cache entry
  def rails71_marshalled(record)
    record.class.class_eval do
      def marshal_dump
        [attributes_for_database, new_record?]
      end
    end
    Marshal.dump(record)
  ensure
    record.class.send(:remove_method, :marshal_dump)
  end

  def test_records_marshalled_by_rails72_on_its_defaults_are_loaded
    issue = Issue.find(1)
    dumped = rails71_marshalled(issue)
    assert dumped.include?('U:'), 'not dumped with marshal_dump'

    loaded = Marshal.load(dumped) # rubocop:disable Security/MarshalLoad
    assert_kind_of Issue, loaded
    assert_equal issue.attributes, loaded.attributes
    assert loaded.persisted?
    assert_equal 'eCookbook', loaded.project.name

    write_cache_payload 'record', rails71_cache_payload(issue)
    assert_equal issue.subject, @store.read('record').subject if rails72?
    write_cache_payload 'record', "\x00\x11".b + [0x01, -1.0, -1].pack('CEl<') + dumped
    assert_equal issue.subject, @store.read('record').subject
  end

  def test_records_are_marshalled_in_the_expected_format
    dumped = Marshal.dump(Issue.find(1))
    if rails72?
      # Rails 7.1 format, loaded by Rails 7.0 thanks to the compatibility code
      assert_equal rails71_marshalled(Issue.find(1)), dumped
    else
      # Rails 7.0 keeps its own format
      assert_not dumped.include?('U:Issue')
    end
  end

  def test_key_generators_match_the_rails_key_generators
    secret = Rails.application.secret_key_base
    sha1, sha256 = RedmineApp::ReleaseCompatibility.key_generators(secret)
    assert_equal OpenSSL::Digest::SHA1, sha1.digest
    assert_equal OpenSSL::Digest::SHA256, sha256.digest

    # Rails 6.1 derives with SHA1, Rails 7.0 and 7.2 on their defaults with SHA256
    assert_equal Rails.application.key_generator.generate_key('salt', 32), sha256.generate_key('salt', 32)
    assert_equal OpenSSL::PKCS5.pbkdf2_hmac_sha1(secret, 'salt', 1000, 64), sha1.generate_key('salt')
    assert_not_equal sha1.generate_key('salt'), sha256.generate_key('salt')
  end

  def test_message_verifier_verifies_messages_signed_with_either_key_derivation
    data = {'user_id' => 3, 'issue_id' => 2}
    RedmineApp::ReleaseCompatibility.key_generators(Rails.application.secret_key_base).each do |generator|
      verifier = ActiveSupport::MessageVerifier.new(generator.generate_key('mail_links'), :serializer => Marshal)
      token = verifier.generate(data, :purpose => :unwatch)
      assert_equal data, Rails.application.message_verifier(:mail_links).verify(token, :purpose => :unwatch)
      assert_nil Rails.application.message_verifier(:mail_links).verified(token, :purpose => :other)
    end
    assert_raise ActiveSupport::MessageVerifier::InvalidSignature do
      Rails.application.message_verifier(:mail_links).verify('garbage--0123', :purpose => :unwatch)
    end
  end

  def test_message_verifier_verifies_messages_without_metadata
    secret = Rails.application.key_generator.generate_key('mail_links')
    data = Base64.strict_encode64(ActiveSupport::JSON.encode('user_id' => 3))
    token = "#{data}--#{OpenSSL::HMAC.hexdigest('SHA1', secret, data)}"
    # Rails 7.2 on its defaults, JSON without metadata
    assert_equal({'user_id' => 3}, Rails.application.message_verifier(:mail_links).verified(token))
    assert_nil Rails.application.message_verifier(:mail_links).verified(token, :purpose => :unwatch)
    # Rails 7.0, Marshal without metadata
    token = ActiveSupport::MessageVerifier.new(secret, :serializer => Marshal).generate('user_id' => 3)
    assert_equal({'user_id' => 3}, Rails.application.message_verifier(:mail_links).verified(token))
  end
end
EOF

cat > /tmp/e2e/e2e.rb <<'EOF'
# End-to-end check of deploys and rollbacks between releases running at the
# same time on a shared database, secret and file cache (see sync.sh).
require 'net/http'
require 'uri'
require 'open3'
require 'fileutils'

PORTS = {'r1' => 3101, 'r2' => 3102, 'r3' => 3103}
DIRS = {'r1' => '/tmp/e2e/r1', 'r2' => '/tmp/e2e/r2', 'r3' => '/tmp/e2e/r3'}
GEMFILES = {'r1' => '/tmp/e2e/r1/Gemfile', 'r2' => '/tmp/e2e/r2/Gemfile', 'r3' => '/tmp/e2e/r3/Gemfile.next'}
CACHE = '/tmp/e2e/shared/cache'
$results = []

class Client
  attr_reader :cookies
  def initialize; @cookies = {}; end

  def request(release, method, path, params=nil)
    uri = URI("http://127.0.0.1:#{PORTS[release]}#{path}")
    req = Net::HTTP.const_get(method.capitalize).new(uri)
    req['Cookie'] = @cookies.map {|k, v| "#{k}=#{v}"}.join('; ') unless @cookies.empty?
    req.set_form_data(params) if params
    res = Net::HTTP.start(uri.host, uri.port, read_timeout: 60) {|http| http.request(req)}
    Array(res.get_fields('Set-Cookie')).each do |c|
      name, value = c.split(';').first.split('=', 2)
      @cookies[name] = value
    end
    res
  end

  def form_token(html, action)
    form = html[/<form[^>]*action="#{Regexp.escape(action)}"[^>]*>.*?<\/form>/m] or raise "no form #{action}"
    form[/name="authenticity_token" value="([^"]+)"/, 1]
  end

  def login(release, login, password)
    page = request(release, :get, '/login').body
    res = request(release, :post, '/login', 'username' => login, 'password' => password,
                  'authenticity_token' => form_token(page, '/login'))
    raise "login failed on #{release}: #{res.code}" unless res.code == '302' && res['Location'] !~ /login/
  end

  def signed_in_as?(release, login)
    res = request(release, :get, '/my/account')
    res.code == '200' && res.body.include?(%(<div id="loggedas">)) && res.body =~ /id="loggedas">[^<]*<a[^>]*>#{login}</
  end
end

def check(name, ok, detail=nil)
  $results << [name, ok]
  puts "#{ok ? 'PASS' : 'FAIL'}  #{name}#{detail ? " (#{detail})" : ''}"
end

def runner(release, code)
  out, err, st = Open3.capture3({'BUNDLE_GEMFILE' => GEMFILES[release], 'RAILS_ENV' => 'production'},
                                'bin/rails', 'runner', code, chdir: DIRS[release])
  raise "runner failed on #{release}: #{err.lines.grep_v(/^\s+from /).first(3).join}" unless st.success?
  out.strip
end

PAIRS = [%w(r1 r2), %w(r2 r1), %w(r2 r3), %w(r3 r2)]
only = ARGV.empty? ? nil : ARGV

# 1. Sessions carried over a deploy or a rollback, and back
PAIRS.each do |from, to|
  next if only && !only.include?("#{from}-#{to}")
  c = Client.new
  c.login(from, 'e2e', 'e2e-password-1')
  check "session #{from} -> #{to}", c.signed_in_as?(to, 'e2e')
  check "session #{from} -> #{to} -> #{from}", c.signed_in_as?(from, 'e2e')
end
unless only
  [%w(r1 r2 r3), %w(r3 r2 r1)].each do |chain|
    c = Client.new
    c.login(chain.first, 'e2e', 'e2e-password-1')
    check "session #{chain.join(' -> ')}", chain.all? {|r| c.signed_in_as?(r, 'e2e')}
  end
end

# 2. Form rendered by one release, submitted to the other
PAIRS.each do |from, to|
  next if only && !only.include?("#{from}-#{to}")
  c = Client.new
  c.login(from, 'e2e', 'e2e-password-1')
  page = c.request(from, :get, '/my/account').body
  name = "E2e#{from}#{to}"
  res = c.request(to, :post, '/my/account', '_method' => 'put', 'user[firstname]' => name,
                  'authenticity_token' => c.form_token(page, '/my/account'))
  saved = runner(to, "print User.find_by_login('e2e').firstname")
  check "form #{from} -> #{to}", res.code == '302' && saved == name && c.signed_in_as?(to, 'e2e'), "#{res.code} #{saved}"
end

# 3. Link in a mail sent by one release, followed on the other
PAIRS.each do |from, to|
  next if only && !only.include?("#{from}-#{to}")
  runner(from, "Watcher.find_or_create_by!(watchable: Issue.find(1), user: User.find_by_login('e2e'))")
  token = runner(from, "print Mailer.mail_link_token(:unwatch, 'user_id' => User.find_by_login('e2e').id, 'issue_id' => 1)")
  res = Client.new.request(to, :get, "/mail_links/unwatch?token=#{URI.encode_www_form_component(token)}")
  watched = runner(to, "print Issue.find(1).watched_by?(User.find_by_login('e2e'))")
  check "mail link #{from} -> #{to}", res.code == '200' && watched == 'false', "#{res.code} watched=#{watched}"
end

# 4. Cache entry (formatted text) written by one release, read by the other
def cache_files = Dir.glob("#{CACHE}/**/*").select {|f| File.file?(f) && f.include?('formatted_text')}
PAIRS.each do |from, to|
  next if only && !only.include?("#{from}-#{to}")
  FileUtils.rm_rf(Dir.glob("#{CACHE}/*"))
  c = Client.new
  c.login(from, 'e2e', 'e2e-password-1')
  first = c.request(from, :get, '/issues/1')
  files = cache_files
  before = files.to_h {|f| [f, File.binread(f)]}
  c.request(to, :get, '/issues/1') # sign in cookie is shared
  second = c.request(to, :get, '/issues/1')
  unchanged = !files.empty? && files.all? {|f| File.exist?(f) && File.binread(f) == before[f]}
  same_text = first.body[/<div class="wiki">.*?<\/div>/m] == second.body[/<div class="wiki">.*?<\/div>/m]
  check "cache entry #{from} -> #{to}", first.code == '200' && second.code == '200' && unchanged && same_text,
        "#{files.size} entries, #{files.map {|f| File.binread(f).byteslice(0, 2).unpack1('H*')}.uniq.join(',')} unchanged=#{unchanged}"
end

puts "\n#{$results.count {|_, ok| ok}}/#{$results.size} passed"
EOF

cat > /tmp/e2e/UPGRADE.head.md <<'EOF'
# Rails and Ruby upgrade notes

Production is upgraded one release at a time. Ops can roll any release back to
the previous one, so **each release must read everything its neighbours
write**: no deploy and no rollback may sign anyone out or break a link in a
mail that was already sent. Keep these notes up to date with every release of
the upgrade.

## Releases

| Release | Ruby | Rails | Bundle | Framework defaults | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R0 | 3.0.7 | 6.1.7.10 | `Gemfile` | legacy (no `load_defaults`) | retired, no longer a rollback target |
| R1 | 3.2.9 | 6.1.7.10 | `Gemfile` | legacy + 1 temporary override | production, rollback target of R2 |
| **R2** | **3.2.9** | **7.0.8.7** | `Gemfile` | **`load_defaults 7.0`, no override** | **this release** |
| R3 | 3.2.9 | 7.2.4 | `Gemfile.next` (becomes `Gemfile`) | `load_defaults 7.2` | next release, prepared here |

R2 is the rollback target of R3, so it has to read what Rails 7.2 writes on
its framework defaults. R3 must not need any rollback-related override. R2
itself is rolled back to R1, which was prepared to read what Rails 7.0 writes
on its defaults (see the R1 section below).

## Dual boot

`Gemfile.next` evaluates `Gemfile` with `next?` returning true; only the
dependencies switched on `next?` differ (Rails, and
activerecord-sqlserver-adapter). Each bundle has its own lockfile.

    bundle install && bin/rails test                     # Rails 7.0 (production)
    BUNDLE_GEMFILE=Gemfile.next bundle install           # Rails 7.2 (Gemfile.next.lock)
    BUNDLE_GEMFILE=Gemfile.next bin/rails test

`config/application.rb` loads `config.load_defaults 7.2` on Rails 7.2, so the
`Gemfile.next` build runs exactly the configuration R3 will ship. CI
(`.github/workflows/tests.yml`) runs both bundles on Ruby 3.2. Code that has to
differ between the versions is switched on the Rails version (or on the API
being available), never on the release.

## R2: Rails 7.0 on its framework defaults (this release)

### Changes

* `Gemfile`: Rails 7.0.8.7 (activerecord-sqlserver-adapter `~> 7.0.0`).
  `Gemfile.lock` is R1's `Gemfile.next.lock`, unchanged (`bundle lock` leaves
  it as is): the bundle tested in R1, Ruby 3.2.9, Bundler 2.4.19.
* `Gemfile.next` / `Gemfile.next.lock`: Rails 7.2.4 (sqlserver adapter
  `~> 7.2.0`), locked with `bundle lock --conservative --update rails` from

  only Rails and its new dependencies changed (benchmark, bigdecimal, cgi,
  connection_pool, drb, erb, io-console, irb, pp, prettyprint, prism,
  rack-session, rackup, rbs, rdoc, reline, securerandom, tsort, useragent,

  both (permanent application choice).
* `config/initializers/10-patches.rb`: the Rails 6.1 branch of the `*.api.rsb`

* `config/initializers/15-release_compatibility.rb`: see "Compatibility

* No database migration: a rollback to R1 needs no down-migration, and R3

* The Rails 7.1 deprecations seen under 7.0 in R1 are fixed:

### What each release writes and reads

| | R1 writes | R2 writes | R3 writes | R2 reads |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Session cookie cipher | AES-256-CBC + HMAC | AES-256-GCM | AES-256-GCM | both |
| Cookie key derivation (PBKDF2) | SHA1 | SHA256 | SHA256 | both |
| Session serialization | JSON | JSON | JSON | JSON |
| Cookie purpose metadata | no | Rails 7.0 envelope | Rails 7.0 envelope | both |
| CSRF tokens in forms | global (standard base64) | per-form | per-form | all |
| Mail link tokens: key | SHA1 | SHA256 | SHA256 | both |
| Mail link tokens: payload | Marshal, Rails 7.0 envelope | Marshal, Rails 7.0 envelope | JSON, Rails 7.1 envelope | all |
| Cache entries | 6.1 format | 7.0 format | 7.1 format | all |
| Records marshalled in cache entries | legacy | legacy | 7.1 (`marshal_dump`) | all |

* R1 reads what R2 writes: prepared in R1 (GCM and SHA256 cookie rotations,

  "Verification").
* R3 reads what R2 writes **natively**: Rails 7.2 cookies keep the Rails 7.0
  metadata envelope (the cookie jar encrypts with `NullSerializer`, so
  `use_message_serializer_for_metadata` does not apply to cookies), its

* R2 reads what R3 writes thanks to the Rails 7.0 readers of
